lines: The plan sets the hill, but the legs are yours. Telo Ride now lets the rider take over the resistance.
Raise resistance moves the target up one level and sends it. Lower resistance moves it down one.
At thirty-two it stays thirty-two, and at one it stays one. Every change is clamped before it's sent.
Before any target, a nudge starts from the resistance the bike reports. Eight becomes nine.
Picking a level sets it outright. Level twenty is sent as twenty, marked as the rider's own.
A change by hand lasts until the segment ends. When the next one starts, the plan's level applies again.
With the bike away, or refusing control, nothing is sent by hand, and the target stays where it was.
Each command remembers where it came from, the plan or the rider, with its acknowledgement time.
Still to come: the steppers and level bars on the ride screens, switched off with no bike.
Home doesn't change yet, at any width. The rider's changes wait in the engine for the ride screens.
What the tests prove: seven new unit tests, one per row of the requirement, and every spec still green.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
